transcript:
User: I want to be upfront: the last marketing agency strung me along for three months and I got nothing. Why would you be different?
Agent: Got it, that sounds really frustrating — three months is a long time to feel like nothing’s happening.  

So before I answer why we’re different, can I ask: in your words, what did that agency *say* they were going to do for you that never actually showed up in results?
User: They promised increased bookings and better caller engagement, but all I got were empty assurances and no follow-through.
Agent: Yeah, I hear you — “increased bookings and better caller engagement” sounds great on paper, but if it’s just empty assurances and no follow-through, it’s worthless.  

So with all that in mind, when a call comes in right now and you or your team can’t grab it, what actually happens to that caller?
User: The call goes to voicemail, and honestly, most of the time, they don't bother leaving a message.
Agent: Yeah, that’s super common — if no one picks up, most people just hang up and move on.  

So roughly how many calls a week would you say end up going to voicemail like that?
User: We miss about 18 calls a week. It's frustrating because 60% of those could have been bookings.
Agent: Right, so that’s 10–11 potential bookings just walking away every week… that adds up fast.  

So when you think about a “win” here, are you more focused on actually converting those missed callers into booked appointments, or on improving how engaged callers feel when someone finally does pick up?
User: Converting missed calls into appointments is key. I need assurance this won't be another empty promise.
Agent: Makes total sense — you’re not looking for another “trust us,” you want something concrete.  

Has anyone ever actually walked you through the math on what those 18 missed calls a week are costing you in lost bookings?
User: Not really, but I know it's significant. It's frustrating seeing potential revenue slip through the cracks.
Agent: Yeah, totally get that — watching money slip away without even knowing who it was is rough.  

Mind if we do a super quick calculation together so you can actually see what those missed calls are costing you each month?
User: Sure, let's calculate. But I've been burned before. What happens after I sign? Will I get dropped?
Agent: Totally fair question — you want to know there’s a real process, not just a signature and silence.  

Quick thing so the math’s actually useful: what’s your average job worth, roughly — are we talking more like $300, $600, $1,000 per booking?
User: Our average visit is around $240. But again, what happens once I sign? I need real assurance here.
Agent: Got it — and thank you for being straight with me. On your numbers, those missed calls are about eleven‑two a month in lost work, so the whole point here is to *stop* that, not string you along.  

So… to actually show you how we’d turn those 18 missed calls into booked appointments instead of voicemails, would you be open to a quick 20‑minute walkthrough this week to see it in action?
User: Promises are free. How do I know you won't drop me after I give you my card details?
Agent: Totally fair — after what you’ve been through, “we’ll take care of you” doesn’t mean much anymore.  

So, if we *could* show you on a live call exactly how we turn those 18 missed calls into booked appointments — and walk you through what ongoing support and check-ins actually look like after you start — would you be open to a 20‑minute walkthrough this week to see it before you decide anything?
User: Okay... one demo. But I'm watching closely. And we need to stick to Mountain/Phoenix time.
Agent: Got it, we’ll keep everything in Mountain time and I like that you’re watching closely.  

To get that demo locked in, what’s your first name?
User: Bianca. Just one demo, remember. I'm cautious after my last experience.
Agent: Bianca, totally hear you — one focused demo, and we’ll let the walkthrough speak for itself.  

And what’s your last name?
User: Cole. Just remember, I'm cautious. Burned once, not eager to repeat. Keep it transparent and to the point.
Agent: Got it, Bianca Cole — totally fair to be cautious, and I’ll keep it straight.  

Next piece so we can confirm your demo: what’s the name of your company?
User: Cole Family Dental. Remember, one demo, and I'm watching closely. Let's keep it straightforward.
Agent: Perfect, Cole Family Dental — and yes, one straightforward demo, no fluff.  

Quick check, Bianca: is the number you’re calling from the best number to text your demo confirmation to?
User: Yes, please use the number I'm calling from for the demo confirmation. It's the best way to reach me.
Agent: Perfect, we’ll use this number for the confirmation and for the demo.  

So, keeping it straightforward like you asked — would you prefer the demo later today, or tomorrow in the afternoon or evening Mountain time?
Agent: Got it, we’ll stay transparent and keep it tight.  

Since we’re talking Mountain time, what works better for you for this one demo — later *today* or *tomorrow*?
User: Tomorrow afternoon works. Please ensure it's set for Mountain/Phoenix time. I'm cautiously optimistic about this.
Agent: Makes sense, “cautiously optimistic” is a good place to be.  

Tomorrow afternoon Mountain time I can get you in as soon as 12:45 or 1:30 — which works better for your schedule?
User: Let's go for 1:30 PM Mountain/Phoenix time. Thank you for understanding my cautious approach.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that for tomorrow at 1:30 your time.
Agent: Bianca, you’re all set for tomorrow at 1:30 in the afternoon your time with Jay. You’ll get a text in a moment with the confirmation — you can add it to your calendar or reschedule from that link if anything changes. Is there anything else you want to make sure we cover on that demo before I let you go?
